messages:
maria: quick heads-up — profiler on the new node pool shows we keep selecting the generic matmul path even though the cards have tensor cores. attaching microbench results in a sec :grimacing:

maria: ```
hw_signature: sm_86
driver: 525.89
cuda: 12.1
probe_result: tc_probe=false
kernel_choice: matmul_fallback (avg=4.8ms)
expected_tc_kernel: tc_fast (avg=1.2ms)
notes: high KV cache evictions observed around seq transitions
```

kai: hmm. do we know if the driver query failed or the probe microbench mis-ran? @maria did you see any cudaGetDeviceAttribute errors?

devon: we saw a similar thing last quarter on a mixed fleet. root cause was a race where driver wasn't loaded fully before our probe ran on boot, so the microbench returned noisy timings and the heuristic marked TC as absent.

asha: this is showing up in production as increased p50 token latency for short-heavy streams. also saw KV eviction spikes when requests jump from seqlen 1 -> 128. small bursts cause cache churn and then we fall back to slow kernels while the cache re-populates.

infra-bot: autoscaler: added 12 instances to pool-nyc-2 at 2026-03-15T03:12:09Z — these are the nodes showing the anomaly.

kai: two quick mitigations: 1) make the device detection resilient to early-boot driver latency (retry short sleep + re-run microbench), 2) if microbench variance > 15% mark device as "unknown" and recheck after N requests with an online microprobe.

devon: we already have a per-device microbench but sampling is 1/100 requests. for new pools that ramp fast we should bump sampling to 1/5 for the first 10k requests, and record per-seqlen probes (1, 16, 64, 256) so kernel picks are seqlen-aware.

asha: proposal: also add seqlen-gating hysteresis — only flip to a heavy-kernel path if 90% of last 500 samples (sliding window) prefer it. this avoids oscillation when load mixes short and long sequences.

maria: agreed. i'll draft a small runtime patch: runtime/hw-detect: (a) check cuDriverGetVersion + cuDeviceGetAttribute, (b) run on-boot microbench with exponential backoff if device returns inconsistent attributes, (c) enable aggressive sampling for new nodes, (d) seqlen hysteresis window + kv-evict metric integration.

maria: sample perf after microbench fix (local lab): ```
node: sm_86, driver 525.89
before: token latency p50=12.3ms, matmul_fallback avg=4.8ms
after: token latency p50=4.9ms, tc_fast avg=1.1ms
kv_eviction_rate: before=0.9/s after=0.12/s
```

joy-sre: if we change detection behavior we need a migration/rollout plan. can't flip globally or we'll risk regressions on Dedicated nodes. opt-in for existing pools + enable for new pools by default? also need telemetry flags for rollback.

devon: rollout plan sounds good: default=false for existing pools, default=true for new pools. canary at 5% of traffic for 48h, auto-roll back on token-latency regression >5%.

kai: small note — persist the per-device microbench fingerprint to /run/redwood/hw_fingerprint.json and include driver+kernel picks in metrics so we can audit misclassifications later.

maria: i'll open a PR with three patches: `hw-detect: boot probe retries`, `sampling: surge-sample-for-new-nodes`, `seqlen-hysteresis + kv-evict-influence`. will add tests and a perf dashboard for canary. 

asha: :thumbsup: thanks. can you add a synthetic test that toggles seq pattern to validate hysteresis doesn't block legitimate switches?

maria: yep, synthetic test + perf numbers included. cc @kai @devon for review.

devon: ok adding to my queue. if we get the microbench stable this should cut p50 by ~50% on affected sm86 fleet and stop KV thrash.

maria: filing tracking issue: https://redwood.internal/issue/INF-2319 (will attach traces & perf dumps).
